planting.note: WARNING: Like other named Callery pear cultivars, sale and planting is now limited or banned in a growing number of states; confirm local rules before planting.

directions: Chanticleer was the first of the narrow-crowned Callery pear selections, patented from a chance seedling found in Cleveland, Ohio in the mid-1960s, well before 'Cleveland Select' and other similarly tight clones entered the trade under their own names. Its upright, oval-to-pyramidal form and strong narrow branch angles resist the storm breakage that plagues the older, broader-crowned 'Bradford', while still producing the same heavy flush of white flowers on bare branches ahead of the leaves each spring. Glossy foliage colors up in orange, red, and burgundy late in fall, often holding later into the season than most other ornamental pears. As with other named Callery pear cultivars, it cross-pollinates readily with nearby selections and sets abundant viable seed that birds spread into wild areas, so its sale and planting are now restricted or banned in a growing number of states.
